title: Match Split
description: A match split continues a graphic line or motion across a divide, so one contour belongs to two worlds at once. One side of the join is a pane or half-frame; the other is its partner; the shared edge, horizon, or gesture is the match.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A table edge runs from a 1960s kitchen into a present-day diner. A face is halved: left is the party you imagined, right is the party you got.
One line, two worlds. Use it when a split should feel like one organism rather than two televisions.

It is the wrong tool when the panes have no shared contour and are only simultaneous: that is ordinary Split Screen. It is also the wrong tool when you cut from one full frame to another rhyming full frame: that is a Match Cut or Graphic Match.
The divide is not a scratch. It is a designed seam that the eye can follow.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Compose both halves so a line, eyeline, horizon, or motion vector continues across the boundary. Match scale of heads if two versions of one person share a couch.
Keep lighting motivated per world unless the gag is that light also matches. Prompt: match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for twins, double lives, expectation versus reality, a road that is two times of day. Do not use it if the two spaces should not touch graphically.
If you need a phone call with frankly separate rooms, a clean split is enough.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Parent Trap seats two versions of one girl in a shared graphic so the split is a relationship. (500) Days of Summer divides a party into expectation and reality along a readable seam.
Use the continued line, not the plot.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space. Name the shared contour (horizon, table, eyeline), what each half contains, and that both are simultaneous.
For video, two plates, one continued line, a stable boundary. No morph across the seam.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a generic Split Screen with unmatched eyelines, or a Match Cut in sequence. The tell: two stacked clips with no shared line, or a cut instead of a co-present seam.
The fix: design the divide, continue one contour, hold both worlds at once.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Match Split in film?
A match split is a divided frame where a line, motion, or contour continues from one world into the other. Both sides of the join are visible together and graphically related.
Match Split vs Split Screen
Split screen shows two fields at once. Match split is a split that rhymes or continues a line across the seam. All match splits are splits; not all splits match.
When should I use Match Split?
Use it when one contour should belong to two worlds at the same time. Do not use it for a simple phone-call panel with no shared geometry.
How do I prompt Match Split for AI image or video?
Name the continued line and both halves. Example: Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space. Simultaneous panes, no morph.
